correctness.rationale: For every odd m>=1 the 4m-vertex circumradius-one regular polygon has apothem c=cos(pi/(4m)) and c B2 subset P subset B2, hence Euclidean norm <= polygonal gauge <= Euclidean norm/c. For unit x,y, the parallelogram identity yields min(N(x+y),N(x-y))<=sqrt(2)/c. Every quarter-turn pair of polygon vertices has both sum and difference on edge normals because m is odd, giving equality. Any achieving pair forces both Euclidean chord norms sqrt(2), both original vectors of Euclidean length 1, so polygon vertices, and dot(x,y)=0. Those vertices are exactly (v_j, +/-v_{j+m}); converse holds, including square m=1. The full equality proof is complete, analytic and all-quantified.
